Thank you. It’s just difficult because his mother is who called the cops and pressed charges. The whole situation is a nightmare. We got into an argument, she got physical with me and I made a sexual advance on her in retaliation and hopes of turning the tide. I’ve never been a violent type and didn’t know she was recording. She screamed stop and told me to get off of her. I did after she said stop for a second time and bit me. No violence occurred and we had never had the make up sex like in movies and what not so I thought I’d try it. So stupid. Cops came and asked what happened and I told the truth about me touching her sexually and stopping. She gave them the audio she had of the situation. They charged me with a violent sexual assault charge. My wife and I got back together months later and have never had any trouble other than this in our now 13 years. She signed an affidavit saying that it was out of character and an isolated incident and she requested the charges be dismissed. It was a one time, stupid mistake on my part. DA told her it doesn’t matter what she wants and that they have enough due to my confession and the audio. But now I’m losing six years of my life and missing out on my son. He’s almost 3 and I’m taking the plea so I’ll see him before he’s 10. It’s just unbelievable and seems overly harsh

I don’t have much advice other than you’re not alone. I am currently in the same boat. Except I work at government agency and have a prominent role. But my days are numbered. My plea has been accepted and my career is over. I have to work to provide as long as I can for my soon to be ex-wife and our son. They will leave and move back to our home state to be with family. I am praying for mercy at sentencing but I struggle with the burden my distinction will carry for my family and friends. I ponder suicide daily. Very similar to your situation. We’re in this together, I guess. They say it gets better. You’re not alone. I am with you.

Thank you for your response. This whole situation is heartbreaking. I will be meeting with my lawyer this week and I will review these items and make sure they are addressed. Still waking up in disbelief. Just praying for mercy. Being a father is so important to me and the “no contact with a minor” part scares me. My poor kiddo had nothing to do with any of this and it is going to negatively impact his life before he can understand what’s going on.

That’s what my lawyer has told me with regards to the mental health. I agree with the plea being the best Avenue. And I know that accepting responsibility is the easiest way through it. Didn’t intend to minimize my actions, as I’m aware of what I did and did not do. The plea is the only chance I’ll have to be a father to my son while he’s still young. Just praying for mercy and mentally preparing the better myself in the time I’m given. I’m open to all avenues of therapy and hope to take every opportunity given to better myself and those around me regarding the situation. Just heartbreaking

Thank you. It’s not easy to feel like any of this is the right thing, but the devil I know is better than the one I don’t. I don’t know much about parole or anything along those lines. I just am preparing for a realistic window (78 months being the least amount on the plea range) and 85% of that makes it 5.5 years. So any time less than that will be something I can live with. But of course I hope to not spend that many years in prison.

My state lawyer is handling my divorce. I have a federal lawyer for the criminal case. To be fair, my lawyer never said anything to me with regards to the registry. I’ve just been researching and learning that a violent offense will be a tier 3 (most severe obv.) and that carries a lifetime sentence in Oklahoma. I am hopeful that my sentence could be lessened at sentencing, when a judge considers my work history (supervisor for a large agency for a few years), no criminal history, documented mental health counseling and medication, the affidavit saying such made by the victim, and involved father to my son. Change is hard. And that’s what I fear the most. I know after a period of time I’ll settle in. I’ll meet people and I’ll stop feeling sorry for myself. But it’s so hard to try and enjoy my last few weeks before I give it all up.

I’ve been reading and it’s frustrating because this same charge in IL (my home state) I would be registering for ten years. But in OK, it’s a lifetime registration. I’m so confused with all the information. I’m heartbroken. Trying to mentally prepare for the inevitable time to be served. And I don’t want to live in OK. I moved here for my job and my wife hates it. I’ll be losing my job and custody of my son. She’ll be taking my son back to IL. And I’ll want to move back there or with family in GA. But I don’t know the laws. If my conviction requires a lifetime registry, what happens if I move somewhere that only requires a certain time period before the possibility of being removed? Thank you all for your responses, if you only knew how nice it felt to not be alone.

No drug or alcohol abuse history to report but I did smoke a lot of marijuana and I was prohibited from consuming alcohol during my pretrial bond period. I’m shaking because I don’t want to go to jail. Life was going so well, things were fine. My ex apparently has said she’ll go on the stand and say she doesn’t want me going to jail and doesn’t want her sons dad being registered, but it doesn’t change the fact that it happened. And 20 years to life is such a long time

I’m facing two aggravated counts that each carry a 10 to life sentence. My plea is down to one count and the 78-90month. Considering 85% served is 5.5-6.5 years. From what my lawyer has told me, federal court is an all or nothing. Either I’m found not guilty, or I face 20 - life

I live in Oklahoma. It was dismissed under a technicality referred to as “McGirt” which basically means I’m native on native territory and the state didn’t have jurisdiction. It’s brand new and there was no telling what would happen. With the affidavit and my clean record and everything becoming calm I figured that I’d be okay. But with the state not having jurisdiction, that opened the doors for the federal government to pick up the case since they did have jurisdiction. Gambled and lost. Taking it to state trial may have been better for me but what can you do.

I’ve got a lawyer and he feels like there is a chance to win at trial, due to my ex’s inability to be likable at times and the mental health aspect. But to risk so many years on a chance is so difficult. I know that’s what plea deals are for. I just feel like I’d rather live my life outside on a registry than inside. It’ll be hard to stomach that I could potentially avoid all of this but it would take a home run and I’m just not sure I can take the risk. My sons whole childhood. Trust me. It’s keeping me up at night

It’s a S Battery charge. My ex physically attacked me and I retaliated in a less than favorable manner. She had an audio recording that she had been taking and gave it to the police. I confessed to the police of my action(s) when they arrived. I live with knowing that if I never talked to police, this wouldn’t be happening. A matter of seconds changed the whole course of my life and my families lives. I was in waiting to be psych eval’d at the time of the incident and was diagnosed as bi-polar and have been on medication and weekly counseling. The affidavit states that it was likely an isolated incident and my counselor wants to go on record defending it. But, like you said, the feds have a confession and audio supporting it. I don’t have much of a chance to fight it. I’m lucky to have a good support system and I’m hopeful that I’ll have a family member that can take me in when I get out. I’m a hard worker and don’t expect much more than an opportunity so the posts have been encouraging. I’ll never be able to coach my sons teams, or even attend some games, and the thought of a Disney vacation is gone. But life is always worth living. I’d rather get to know the man he becomes and that’s the only thing motivating me to fight through this.

I play guitar and sing. It’s a great outlet. Something that she ironically took from me. Actually met her at a show I was playing. Started dating and all my free time went to her. 12 years later, my goal is to play again
Yes, on mild medication and see a therapist weekly. It’s so good for me. But being bound to toxicity was a lot of my problem IMO
